item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00339","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C06","C16","C04"],"selected_candidate_label":"C06","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C06 plausibly supplied a concrete and material template. Both directives address the same Public Law 874 school program, distinguish federally operated schools from schools connected to state authority, and organize the policy around integration on federally owned military property. The child operationalizes the precise policy and administrative distinction articulated in C06: direct federal responsibility supports integration, while state-operated schools on federal property require engagement with local authorities and possible alternative arrangements. C16 shares only the broader federal-versus-state education theme, and C04 contains only a general nondiscrimination rule in an unrelated selective-service scheme.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"all schools operated by the Army under provisions of Section 6 of Public Law 874 will be on a completely integrated basis","parent_excerpt":"schools operated solely by the Federal Government on Federally-owned land","explanation":"Both focus on federally operated schools on federal property and the federal government's direct responsibility for their integration."},{"child_excerpt":"schools by state authorities on Federally-owned property under the provisions of Section 3 of Public Law 874","parent_excerpt":"Public Laws No. 815 and 874 ... schools on Federal property","explanation":"The documents concern the same statutory program and the same distinctive setting of schools located on federal property."},{"child_excerpt":"Army commanders are in the process of making a survey ... designed to bring about agreement with local authorities for integrating the schools. If such integration is not achieved, other arrangements ... will be considered.","parent_excerpt":"It is never our purpose to insist on integration without considering pertinent local factors; but it is the duty of the Federal Government to move forward ... under individual conditions and circumstances.","explanation":"The child converts C06's stated approach—pursuing integration while accounting for local conditions—into a concrete survey, negotiation, and contingency process."}]}
